text:
Maria L.: Heads up — after yesterday's continuous-batching change I see a 12% latency p95 regression and prefix cache hit-rate dropped from 48% -> 31% on prod-gpu pool. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

Kevin P.: saw spikes, linking traces now

Maria L.: trace: /traces/abc123 — key observations: queue depth up, batch sizes skewed to mixed prefixes leading to low cache reuse

Sam O.: can you paste the sampling profiler output? curious about kernel selection

Maria L.: pasted:
```json
{"sampled_kernels": {"fast_attn_v2": 62, "fallback_fma": 38}, "avg_batch_size": 9.2, "prefetch_hit": 0.31}
```

Perf Bot: perf-alert: prefix_cache_hit_rate dropped 48->31% on cluster-prod-gpu-7 in 5m window. p95 latency +12%

Kevin P.: that fallback_fma bump is suspicious — kernel selector probably changed path because of varying seq_len distribution in batches

Rachel T.: we changed continuous-batching weighting to favor fill-rate; it may be mixing long prefix requests with short ones. That reduces prefix coalescing.

Sam O.: agree. continuous batching groups by time, not prefix. If we get a few long-prefix requests early they drag other requests into same batch and ruin cache reuse.

Maria L.: reproduction on staging: reduce batch timeout -> hit-rate back to 46% and p95 improves. Quick diff:
```
- continuous.batch.timeout_ms: 15
+ continuous.batch.timeout_ms: 8
```

Kevin P.: interesting. But lowering timeout hurts throughput. Need better heuristic: group by prefix fingerprint first, then fill

Rachel T.: proposal: change batcher to maintain small in-flight per-prefix buckets (hot buckets) and prefer coalescing into them up to N or T. Fallback to cross-prefix merging after threshold.

Sam O.: also consider changing cache keying: include prompt-prefix-length bucket so short/long don't collide in same cohort. Might increase key diversity though.

Maria L.: perf tradeoffs: simulated on production traces: adding hot-buckets recovered hit-rate to 44% and p95 to +3% vs baseline, throughput down 1.5%.

Kevin P.: can we try kernel-aware batch composition? prefer grouping requests that align on kernel selection (same seq_len range) so we don't trigger fallback kernels within a batch

Rachel T.: good idea. We can use cheap pre-routing: seq_len estimate from tokenized prompt length. Runtime profiler can mark kernel fallback freq per cohort.

Perf Bot: suggestion recorded: run A/B with hot-buckets + kernel-aware grouping on prod-canary 10% traffic

Maria L.: I'll spin canary tomorrow AM. I'll dump heatmap and sample traces in thread once available.

Sam O.: thx. if anyone has quick experiments to run on staging ping me — I have a script to emulate request arrival patterns

Maria L.: thanks all :rocket:
